name: Aghori
body:
While most necromancers work their art using arcane or divine power, aghori employ the power of their own souls and the energies of the cosmos. An aghori understands that all things within the material world are merely illusions, belying a greater truth. In their philosophy there is no greater illusion than the trinity of life, death, and undeath. For the good of all, they diligently tread on these hollow concepts.

Parent Class: White Necromancer.

Class Atavism: Aghoris represents an ancient precursor to modern white necromancers. This class occurs rarely in the modern era, but occupies the same niche as the white necromancer. An aghori counts as a white necromancer for the purposes of fulfilling any non-spellcasting related prerequisites.

System Akashic Starcalling

Role: Aghori are starcallers who study the interplay between mortal existence and the stars. They see through the falsehood of life’s eternal cycle, which some call the “necromantic triad”. This gives them the power to preserve life and defy the iron grip of death. Their mastery of stellar energies allows them to summon tools and creatures to aid them in their work.

Alignment: Any non-evil

Hit Die: d6

Starting Wealth: 2d6 × 10 gp (average 70 gp). In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The aghoris’s class skills are Appraise (Int), Craft (Int), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (arcana) (Int), Knowledge (religion) (Int), Profession (Wis), Sense Motive (Wis), Spellcraft (Int), and Use Magic Device (Cha).

Skill Ranks Per Level: 2 + Int modifier

Table: Aghori
Level	Base Attack Bonus	Fort Save	Ref Save	Will Save	Special	Essence

Class Features

The following are the class features of this class.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

Aghoris are proficient with all simple weapons. They are not proficient with any type of armor or shield.

Constellations

Aghori learn to call on the constellations for power starting at 1st level The constellations that they can manifest are drawn from a single cosmology as described in the cosmology ability. They use Wisdom as their starcalling modifier. The saving throw DCs for their constellations is 10 + 1/2 their starcaller level + their starcalling modifier unless stated otherwise.

Deathly Interlocutor (Ex)

Aghori gain the extraordinary ability to see doom marks, and gain necril as a bonus language.

Lore of Life and Death (Ex)

An aghori adds their Wisdom modifier, in addition to their Intelligence modifier, when making Knowledge (religion) skill checks pertaining to subjects involving death, burial practices, undead, or the afterlife. In addition, an aghori gains a bonus equal to 1/2 their aghori level (minimum +1) to all Heal skill checks.

Rebuke Death And Life (Sp)

As a standard action, an aghori can touch a creature to heal it for 1d4 hp. They can use this ability only on a living creature that is below 0 hp; or on an undead creature that is below 5 hp. Alternatively, they can expend an additional use of this ability when activating it to deal 1d4 points of untyped damage to a living or undead creature they touch (DC 10 + their Charisma modifier + 1 for each point of essence invested in this ability; Will for half). This damage is the result of a disruption of a creature’s living or undead state; it can’t be resisted in any way, such as by damage reduction or immunities.They can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + their Charisma modifier.

Starting at 2nd level, this ability can be invested with essence. For each point of essence invested in this ability, the healing or damage it causes increases by 1.

Cairn-Called Elements

Constellations summoned by an aghori carry echoes of the grave. This imparts unique properties on an aghori’s constellations based on their elements. All constellations manifested by the aghori are augmented as follows, but still otherwise count and function as being their normal element:

All Elements

All of the aghori’s constellations gain the following properties based on their manifestation type. This is in addition to any properties granted due to its element:

All: The aghori’s constellations have muted colors and are slightly translucent. This inflicts a circumstance penalty of -1 on all attempts to detect, perceive, or identify an aghori’s constellations. Creatures with the ability to see doom marks ignore this penalty and instead gain a +1 circumstance bonus on such checks.
Champion: For the purposes of effects targeting creatures by type (such as a ranger’s favored enemy and bane weapons), the aghori’s champion manifestations count as both their normal type and undead. They can be affected by effects that specifically target undead, such as halt undead. Though, they are still affected by positive and negative energy as normal for a creature of their type. However, the aghori’s champions gain a +4 insight bonus on Fortitude saves against effects that could not normally affect objects or undead, and take only half damage from bleed effects (round down; minimum 1).
Æther (Self)

In the translation of one’s being, from life to death, the element of “Æther” becomes a conduit for the “Self”. The aghori’s constellations with the æther element gain the following properties based on their manifestation type:

All: All constellations of this element are more firmly rooted in existence. The DCs to dispel, disjoin, or remove these constellations is increased by +1. Additionally, the aghori gain a +1 competence bonus to opposed checks made to resist the attempts to forcibly dismiss their constellations (e.g. the card keeper zodiac’s seal/banish constellation ability), “self” element constellations also gain this bonus on saving throws to resist being dismissed.
Air (Breath)

The touch of the hereafter transmutes the element of “Air” into the ultimate sigh of “Breath”. The aghori’s constellations with the air element gain the following properties based on their manifestation type:

Armor: The DC to locate or track the wearer by scent is increased by an amount equal to half the aghori’s Wisdom modifier (minimum 1).
Champion/Sign: The Champion, or the marked, gains a + 5 ft. enhancement bonus to all of their movement speeds.
Equipment/Instrument/Weapon: The DC of attempts to disarm, dispel, steal, or sunder these constellation manifestations is increased by an amount equal to half the aghori’s Wisdom modifier (minimum 1).
Earth (Grave Dirt)

The touch of the hereafter transmutes the element of “Earth” into the fragrant darkness of “Grave Dirt”. The aghori’s constellations with the earth element gain the following properties based on their manifestation type:

Armor/Equipment(worn): The wearer gains a + 1 deflection bonus to AC against incorporeal touch attacks. Additionally, incorporeal, ethereal, and quasi-real creatures treat any squares in 5 ft. radius emanation centered on the wearer as difficult terrain.
Champion/Sign: The champion, or the marked, gains DR/bludgeoning and magic equal to half the aghori’s Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). Equipment (all other)/Instrument/Weapon: These manifestations gain a bonus to their hardness equal to half the aghori’s Wisdom modifier (minimum 1).
Fire (Soul)

The touch of the hereafter transmutes the element of “Fire” into the ephemeral flame of “Soul”. The aghori’s constellations with the fire element gain the following properties based on their manifestation type:

Armor/Champion/Sign: If the champion, wearer, or the marked takes negative energy damage to their hit points, a number of points of that damage equal to a maximum of half the aghori’s Wisdom modifier (minimum 1) are instead converted to an equal amount of healing.
Armor (shield)/Equipment/Instrument: These manifestations are wreathed in motes of pale flame causing them to cast light as a candle. This light is only visible to the creature in possession of the manifestation, undead, and creatures that can see doom marks.
Weapon: Deal a number of additional points of force damage equal to half the aghori’s Wisdom modifier (minimum 1) against incorporeal, ethereal, and quasi-real creatures.
Void (Hollow)

The touch of the hereafter transmutes the element of “Void” into the utter absence of “Hollow”. The aghori’s constellations with the void element gain the following properties based on their manifestation type:

All: All constellations of this element can not be identified or have their properties determined by mundane means. Additionally, in order to detect them by magical means a creature must first succeed on a Knowledge (Religion) check (DC= 10 + the aghori’s aghori level). If the check fails, the hollow constellation is detected as non-magical in nature as if it was only a mundane object, creature, or mark of its general type. If the check succeeds, the magical detection functions as normal.
Water (Memory)

The touch of the hereafter transmutes the element of “Water” into the murky lagoon of “Memory”. The aghori’s constellations with the water element gain the following properties based on their manifestation type:

Armor: The wearer gains an insight bonus on Disguise checks equal to half the aghori’s Wisdom modifier (minimum 1).
Champion/Equipment (worn)/Sign: The champion, wearer, or marked gains an insight bonus on saving throws against, fear, emotion, and compulsion effects equal to half the aghori’s Wisdom modifier (minimum 1).
Equipment (all other)/Weapon: The creature wielding or in possession of the manifestation gains an a +1 insight bonus to CMD and on Sleight of Hand checks related to concealing the constellation manifestation.
Instrument: The performer gains a +1 insight bonus to Knowledge checks, and Perception checks made to see through disguises (if they would normally gain a bonus due to familiarity), made while performing with these constellations.
Cosmology

At 1st level, the aghori must select a cosmology to attune themselves to. This must be a cosmology that is tied to their current plane of existence. They must also select any lost constellations or lesser cosmologies that they wish to access at this time (subject to the customization limit rule). Once they have chosen a cosmology, they cannot manifest constellations from another cosmology without taking the Expanded Cosmology feat. If they spend at least one month in a plane with a different cosmology than the one they chose, they may choose to realign themselves with the new cosmology, losing access to their previous cosmology and constellations and gaining access to those available in the new cosmology. Additionally, they gain a competence bonus equal to their starcalling modifier to identify constellation manifestations that are a part of their cosmology.

All as One (Su)

All of the champion forms of the aghori’s constellations have a single shared pool of health points equal to 1d6 + their starcalling modifier, per starcaller level (the 1st d6 is maximized). This replaces any hit points that champions would normally have from HD and class levels, but does not alter their HD total for the purposes of effects based on their number of HD. Any effects that add to or subtract from a champion’s hit points (e.g. the Toughness feat, the essence effect of The Boar’s champion form, or Constitution damage) are applied to this shared pool for the effect’s duration on until the champion that is the source of the effect is dismissed, whichever happens first. Constitution damage, drain, or increases taken by a champion alter the shared pool’s maximum hit points while the affected champion is summoned as if the score that determines the aghori’s starcalling modifier had been had taken damage or drain, or been increased by the same amount.

All damage, healing, and temporary hit points received by champions are deducted from or added to this shared pool. When the pool is reduced to 0 or below, all champions manifested by the aghori are dismissed, and may not be manifested again until the pool is returned to a positive value. If this shared pool has been reduced to 0, it is automatically restored to half of its normal maximum value after 24 hours.

All of aghori’s champions count as a single entity for beneficial abilities that may only be used on a creature a limited number of times a day (e.g. a witch‘s healing hex).

Should multiple champions take damage from the same attack or effect, the damage is only applied to the shared hit point pool once as if it had only affected the champion that would have taken the most damage.

Life Bond (Su)

At 1st level, the aghori forms a close bond with their champions. As long as the aghori and at least one of their manifested champions are within 100 feet of each other, whenever enough damage would be dealt to their champions’ shared hit point pool to dismiss their champions, as a reaction to the damage, the aghori can sacrifice any number of hit points they have without using an action. Each hit point sacrificed in this way prevents 1 point of damage dealt to their champions’ shared hit point pool. This can prevent champions from being dismissed.

At 5th level, an aghori may create a bond between themself and another living creature within 90 ft. as a standard action. This creature can’t not be a champion manifested by the aghori; champions manifested by another starcaller that are subject to “all as one” or a similar ability that imposes a shared hp pool count as the same creature as all of their starcaller’s other manifested champions as described in the ability. They may have one bond active per aghori level -1. Each round at the start of the aghori’s turn, if a bonded creature is wounded for 5 or more hp below its maximum hp, the bonded creature heals 5 hp and the aghori takes 5 hp damage. This bond continues until the bonded creature dies, the aghori dies, the distance between them exceeds 90 ft., or the aghori ends it as an immediate action. If they have multiple bonds active, they may end as many as they want as part of the same immediate action.

Essence Pool

At 1st level, the aghori gains access to a pool of essence which can be invested into their constellations and other essence receptacles to increase their power.The pool of available essence is listed in the aghori’s class table. As a swift action, the aghori can reallocate their essence investments into or between their constellations and other essence receptacles.

Virasata (Su)

At 1st level, the aghori gains the ability to summon an ancestral animal spirit known as a virasata to aid them in their labors. This ability functions and counts as the legendary spiritualist‘s phantom and etheric tether class features, and a virasata functions like and counts as a phantom, except as described here.

Essence can be bound to this ability. The aghori is treated as having an effective spiritualist level for determining their virasata’s statistics and their etheric tether’s effects equal to 2 x the number of points of essence bound to this ability (minimum level 1; to a maximum level equal to the aghori’s class level). They can take a point of essence burn as a swift or immediate action to extend their etheric tether by 10 feet for 1 minute. This effect stacks with itself. Essence burn taken in this way can not be recovered until this effect ends.

While the aghori’s virasata is confined within their consciousness, the aghori gains a +1 competence bonus on Will saving throws, Sense Motive checks, and to the DCs of their class abilities and constellation effects against creatures that protect the cycle of life, death, and rebirth (e.g. psychopomps, marut inevitables, akhana aeons, clerics with the repose domain, and scion of the veil spiritualists).

A virasata has the following unique abilities and traits:

The virasata always takes the form of an animal.
A virasata does not have an emotional focus (or the associated focus powers and other benefits of an emotional focus), does not gain a phantom’s normal DR while in its ectoplasmic form, nor does it gain the share spells or deliver touch spell abilities.
A virasata’s good saves are always Will and Fortitude, and its bad save is Reflex
A virasata refuses to manifest in the presence of a champion manifested by the aghori it’s bonded with. Furthermore, if a virasata is manifested when such a creature is summoned, it immediately retreats into its aghori’s consciousness, and will not manifest again until all of its aghori’s champions are dismissed.

The virasata gains the following abilities at the indicated levels:

Mirror Constellations (Su)

At 1st level, as long as it is within 10 feet of the aghori, the virasata gains gains a copy of a single constellation (armor[except shields], equipment [worn], sign, and weapon forms only) that the aghori is currently wearing, wielding, or is marked by that they manifested. This includes the effects of any invested essence or applied metaconstellation feats. The virasata’s copy of an armor and equipment manifestation appears already equipped to it; a sign appears already marking them; and a weapon is channeled into one of its natural weapons as if via the Weapon Fusion feat.

The aghori can change this constellation as a standard action or a part of manifesting a new constellation. If the aghori dismiss a constellation shared in this way, or if the virasata leaves the range of this ability, it loses its copy of the shared constellation until it is once again in range and the aghori spend a standard action to grant it a copy of a constellation they currently have manifested.
Grave Element Focus (Su)

At 1st level, the virasata gains additional abilities from its bond to the elements of the hereafter. The aghori selects one of the following cairn-called elements, and their virasata is augmented based on this choice. Once this choice is made it can not be changed.

Breath: The virasata gains a number of ranks in Acrobatics or Sleight of Hand equal to its number of Hit Dice (once this choice is made it can’t be changed). The selected skill becomes a class skill for the virasata if it isn’t already. Additionally, the virasata gains Run as a bonus feat.
Grave Dirt: The virasata gains a number of ranks in Appraise or Survival equal to its number of Hit Dice (once this choice is made it can’t be changed). The selected skill becomes a class skill for the virasata if it isn’t already. Additionally, as long as it is summoned, its master gains the Ectoplasmic Constellation feat as bonus feat.
Hollow: The virasata gains a number of ranks in Perception or Stealth equal to its number of Hit Dice (once this choice is made it can’t be changed). The selected skill becomes a class skill for the virasata if it isn’t already. Additionally, the virasata gains Lightning Reflexes as a bonus feat
Memory: The virasata gains a number of ranks in Disguise or Knowledge (any) equal to its number of Hit Dice (once this choice is made it can’t be changed). The selected skill becomes a class skill for the virasata if it isn’t already. Additionally, the virasata gains Iron Will as a bonus feat.
Self: The virasata gains a number of ranks in Diplomacy or Perform (any) equal to its number of Hit Dice (once this choice is made it can’t be changed). The selected skill becomes a class skill for the virasata if it isn’t already. Additionally, the virasata gains Great Fortitude as a bonus feat.
Soul: The virasata gains a number of ranks in Heal or Sense Motive equal to its number of Hit Dice. The selected skill becomes a class skill for the virasata if it isn’t already. Additionally, as long as it is summoned, its master gains resistance 5 against negative energy damage.
Cosmic Conduit

At 3rd level, the virasata can deliver a constellation’s sign form, or touch ranged constellation effect, in a similar manner to a familiar delivering a touch spell or hex, using the aghori’s relevant saving throw DC.

At 11th level, the aghori’s effective spiritualist level becomes 5 + double the number of points of essence bound to this ability (to a maximum equal to the aghori’s aghori level).
Improved Essence Capacity

At 3rd level and every six levels thereafter, the aghori’s skill at investing essence improves and the total essence capacity of all their essence receptacles increases by 1

Power Over Undead (Su)

Beginning at 3rd level, an aghori receives Turn Undead as a bonus feat. They are treated as having the channel energy class ability, but only for purposes of using this feat.

An aghori can channel energy a number of times per day equal to 1 + their Charisma modifier, but only to use the Turn Undead feat. They can take other feats to add to this ability, such as Extra Channel and Improved Channel, but not feats that alter this ability, such as Alignment Channel, Elemental Channel, or Selective Channeling. The DC to save against this feat is 10 + 1/2 their aghori level + their Charisma modifier. When they channel energy, all undead are potentially affected, even those under their control. At 20th level, undead cannot add their channel resistance to the save against this ability.

Stellar Necromancy (Su)

The energies of the stars contain echoes of both positive energy and negative energy. An aghori can refine these echos to restore life or at least a semblance of it. Starting at 4th level, the aghori gains the ability to raise the dead by means of stellar signs. A number of times per day equal to 1 + their Wisdom modifier, they can mark a dead creature with the sign form of a constellation, despite the normal limitation of signs to marking creatures. When raising a dead creature they can choose either imbue it with negative energy or positive energy. The effects of doing so are as follows based on the aghori’s level and function as follows:

Positive Energy (Resurrection)

Except as indicated, the sign used to resurrect a creature can be removed at any time, this has no ill effect on the creature. If a creature resurrected by this ability is marked again with the sign that was used to resurrect it, that sign is treated as being invested with 1 more point of essence than normal. This effect does not stack with itself, or with other virtual essence increases (e.g. the stellar lens magic item). Additionally, the aghori gains an insight bonus on Diplomacy checks equal to their starcalling modifier against a creature that they currently have marked with a sign that was used to resurrect them.

4th Level: The marked corpse is temporarily resurrected as if by raise dead. However, they immediately die if the sign used to resurrect them is removed, or after a number of rounds equal to the aghori’s Wisdom modifier, whichever happens first. A creature can only be resurrected in this way once, and must have been dead for no more than 24 hours.
10th Level: The aghori can expend a diamond worth 5,000 gp as a part of using this ability. If they do so, the marked corpse is restored to life as if by raise dead. Once the corpse is marked, and this ability is used, the creature will return to life after 1 minute.
14th Level: The aghori can expend a diamond worth 10,000 gp as a part of using this ability. If they do so, the marked corpse is restored to life as if by resurrection. Once the corpse is marked, and this ability is used, the creature will return to life after 1 minute.
18th Level: The aghori can expend a diamond worth 25,000 gp as a part of using this ability. If they do so, the marked corpse is restored to life as if by true resurrection. Once the corpse is marked, and this ability is used the creature will return to life after 1 minute.
Negative Energy (Reanimation)

When an aghori reanimates a creature in this way it does not count as an evil act, and the spell effects replicated by this effect lose the evil descriptor. The sign used to reanimate a creature can be removed at any time, this has no ill effect on the undead. If an undead created using this ability is marked again with the sign that was used to reanimate it, that sign is treated as being invested with 1 more point of essence than normal. This does not stack with itself or other virtual essence increases such as the stellar lens magic item. Additionally, the aghori gains an insight bonus on Diplomacy checks equal to their starcalling modifier against an undead that they have marked with the sign that was used to animate it.

Mindless undead resulting from stellar necromancy are of neutral alignment. The alignment of intelligent undead exactly matches the aghori’s alignment.

4th Level: The marked corpse is reanimated as if by animate dead, lesser. As a part of the action to mark a corpse with a sign they must expend an onyx gem worth at least 25 gp per Hit Die of the undead being created. At 6th level this ability instead functions as animate dead.
No matter how many times they use this ability, an aghori can entreat the aid of only 4 HD worth of undead creatures per aghori level they possess. If they exceed this number, they can request the aid of any newly created undead, but any excess undead from previous uses of this ability begin to mindlessly act of their own accord and can’t be asked to provide service or to otherwise assist the aghori as described below. The aghori chooses which creatures lose the capacity to be entreated in this way.
12th: The aghori can spend an hour worth of effort preforming a ritual prior to marking a corpse this ability to have it instead function as create undead. Additionally, the gp value of the onyx gem expended increases to 50 gp per HD of the undead to be created along with any other costs listed in the undead‘s entry. The aghori’s effective caster level, for the purpose of deciding the types undead you can create in this way, is equal to their aghori level.
16th: As the 12th level option, except they gain the ability to create undead available via create greater undead in this way so long as their effective caster level is high enough.

The aghori gains no specific control over undead created using stellar necromancy, although they may ask the undead to provide some service or to otherwise assist them. To make such a request, the aghori must make a special Diplomacy check, rolling 1d20 + the aghori’s level + their Charisma modifier.

Mindless undead created through stellar necromancy initially are indifferent toward the aghori, and a flat DC 15 Diplomacy check is required when requesting their assistance. Intelligent undead initially are friendly toward the aghori, and a flat DC 15 + the creature’s Charisma modifier is required when requesting their assistance.

An aghori must treat any undead created through stellar necromancy with honor and respect at all times. In most cases, an aghori should agree to release the undead once the requested service or task has been completed. Intelligent undead created through stellar necromancy might agree to follow the aghori for a prolonged period of time. In such cases, the undead would certainly expect to be treated as an honored and respected companion, and might even occasionally make requests of its own.

An aghori can release an undead that they have raised in a ritual that takes 1 hour to complete, as long as the undead is mindless or willing. At the end of this ritual the undead is destroyed and the aghori can retrieve from its remains an onyx gem with a gp value equal to half the cost of the gem used to raise it. The aghori can release any number of undead in this manner as a part of the same ritual.

An aghori who fails to properly respect any undead they create suffers a -10 to Diplomacy and similar skill checks when making new requests of that undead, subject to the GM’s discretion. This includes failing to release an undead after it fulfils their request.

At 8th level, the aghori gains the ability to mark a corpse with a sign to prevent a creature from rising as if by rest eternal. Their effective caster level for this effect is equal to their aghori level and they must expend a vial of holy or unholy water as a part of using this ability. If the creature targeted with this effect is later resurrected or reanimated by another creature, the aghori still gains the benefit to Diplomacy checks against the creature when marking them with sign used to initiate the rest eternal effect as if they were they had resurrected or reanimate the creature via stellar necromancy.

Starcaller’s Summons (Su)

At 6th level, as a standard action, the aghori can summon one of their manifested champions of their choice to their side. This functions as dimension door, using the aghori’s starcaller level as the caster level. When this ability is used, the selected champion appears adjacent to the aghori (or as close as possible if all adjacent spaces are occupied). If the selected champion is out of range, the ability is wasted. The aghori can use this ability once per day at 6th level, plus one additional time per day for every four levels beyond 6th.

Necrotic Transfer (Su)

At 7th level, an aghori can transfer some of their life essence to another living creature. As a standard action, when an aghori touches a creature, they can sacrifice a maximum amount of their own hp equal to 10 + their Constitution score + their aghori level. Those hit points are then immediately transferred to the creature touched. These hp heal the subject but cannot raise the subject’s hp higher than its normal hp total.

Voice of the Grave (Su)

At 7th level, an aghori can speak with dead, as the spell, for a number of rounds per day equal to their aghori level. These rounds need not be consecutive. At 9th level, and every two levels thereafter, the Will save DC to resist this effect increases by +1

Elevated Sight (Su)

At 9th level, an aghori gains Elevated Sight as a bonus feat even if they do not meet the prerequisites. The base range of the essence sight ability granted by this feat increases by 5 ft. at 13th level and by an additional 5 ft. for every four levels beyond 13th.

Ghost Walk (Su)

Beginning at 13th level, an aghori can become incorporeal as a standard action. They can use this ability once per day at 13th level and twice per day at 17th level.

While in this form, the aghori can move in any direction and through any object (except for those made of force). They can take no action other than to move while in this form. They remain in this form for a number of rounds equal to their aghori level, but they can end this effect at any time with a standard action.

Death Warded (Su)

At 15th level, an aghori receives a morale bonus equal to half their aghori level on all saves against death spells and death effects. They are granted a save to negate such effects even if one is not normally allowed.

Protective Aura (Su)

At 17th level, the aghori can, as an immediate action, emit a 30 ft. aura that protects against death effects for a number of rounds per day equal to their aghori level. Living creatures within this area are immune to all death spells, death effects, energy drain, and effects that cause negative levels. This protective aura does not remove negative levels that a creature has already gained, but the negative levels have no effect while the creature is inside the protected area. This ability can be invested with essence. For each point of essence invested the radius of this ability increases by 10 ft.

These rounds need not be consecutive.

I Am Become Truth (Su/Sp)

At 20th level, an aghori gains the ability to freely disrupt the concepts of life, death, and undeath. Once per round as a supernatural effect, they can cast bleed, disrupt undead, grave words, or stabilize as a free action. If they are brought to below 0 hp, they automatically stabilize.They also become immune to all death descriptor effects. Ability damage and drain cannot reduce them to below 1 in any ability score. Once per day each, they can use circle of death, breath of life, and undeath to death as spell-like abilities.

Fallen Aghori

An aghori who ceases to be non-evil aligned, or that outrageously dishonors an undead they animated, do not lose their connection to the powers they command. However, their descent into depravity does hamper their abilities. This has the following effects:

They suffer a -5 penalty to Diplomacy and similar skill checks when making requests of undead they have animated.
The essence capacity of all of their class abilities, including their constellations, is reduced by 1.
They lose access to the effects of the life bond ability’s 5th level advancement and the necrotic transfer ability,

These penalties are removed, they regain any lost abilities, and the aghori regains advancement potential if they atone for their violations (see atonement), as appropriate.
